name: marcella eggplant sauce
instructions:
Marcella Hazan's eggplant sauce. Fried eggplant folded into a simple garlic-and-tomato base, tossed with pasta. She specifies SPAGHETTINI as the best pasta pair. Two sub-variants (basic + a built-up ricotta-and-basil version); both untested by me. Described informally.

See sibling recipes in the italian-tomato-sauces folder ([[marcella-tomato-sauce]], [[sicilian-pesto-rosso]], [[vodka-sauce]], [[pasta-piperade]]) for other italian tomato-sauce shapes.

=== VARIANT A — BASIC EGGPLANT SAUCE ===

INGREDIENTS (informal):
- eggplant (~1 medium/large, peeled, sliced)
- vegetable oil (a LOT — 1.5 inches deep in the pan for the fry)
- garlic (a few cloves, sliced or minced)
- canned diced tomatoes (a full can)
- fresh parsley
- red chili flakes
- salt
- spaghettini (Marcella's specified pasta pairing)

PROCEDURE:
1. PREP THE EGGPLANT (Marcella's specific instructions): peel the eggplant and slice it. Salt the slices in a colander and let them sit for 30 min with something under the colander to catch the drippings — the salt draws out bitter/watery liquid. Save the drippings (they're part of Marcella's technique — she uses them, don't discard).
2. FRY THE EGGPLANT: heat 1.5 inches of vegetable oil in a pan (a lot — this is a proper shallow-fry, not a sauté). Fry the eggplant slices until golden and soft inside. Drain on paper towels.
3. MAKE THE SAUCE: in a separate pan, sauté the garlic in a small amount of oil until fragrant. Add the canned diced tomatoes, parsley, red chili flakes, and salt. Simmer to reduce into a sauce.
4. FOLD FRIED EGGPLANT IN AT THE END (don't cook it further in the sauce — you want it to keep its fried texture).
5. TOSS WITH COOKED SPAGHETTINI.

=== VARIANT B — BUILT-UP VERSION (RICOTTA + BASIL) ===

Marcella's more built-up variant of the same recipe. Same base but with these changes:
- WHOLE TOMATOES (canned) instead of a can of diced
- EGGPLANT CUT INTO SMALLER CUBES instead of slices (still fried, still salted first)
- OMITS THE RED CHILI FLAKES
- ADDS FRESH RICOTTA CHEESE (dolloped or folded in with the pasta at the end)
- ADDS FRESH BASIL LEAVES

Otherwise same procedure. The ricotta + basil push it into a richer, more napoli-adjacent register (echoes of pasta alla norma without going full norma).
notes:
Untested by me. Written down as an informal scaffold from Marcella (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant E) into its own file.

=== THE SALT-AND-DRAIN STEP FOR THE EGGPLANT IS LOAD-BEARING (MARCELLA'S TECHNIQUE) ===

Peeling, slicing, salting in a colander for 30 min with something to catch drippings — this is her whole approach to eggplant across recipes. Draws out bitter/watery liquid, so the eggplant fries cleanly (crisp outside, tender inside) instead of soaking up oil like a sponge. The drippings are part of the technique — she uses them, doesn't discard. If you skip this step, the fried eggplant reads soggy and greasy.

--- MODERN EGGPLANTS AREN'T AS BITTER — SALTING MAY BE UNNECESSARY FOR BITTERNESS ---

Marcella's technique was written when eggplants routinely carried real bitterness that needed to be salted out. MODERN COMMERCIAL EGGPLANTS have been bred to be much less bitter — for most eggplants you'll buy today, the bitterness-reduction purpose of the salt-and-drain step is largely moot.

The TEXTURE purpose still holds: salting draws out water, which keeps the eggplant from soaking up oil sponge-like during the fry. If you want the crisp-outside/creamy-inside fried texture, keep the salt step for the water-drawing reason even if bitterness isn't a concern.

IF YOU'RE SHORT ON TIME AND YOUR EGGPLANT LOOKS FRESH: you can probably skip the salt-drain step and go straight to frying. The result won't be quite as crisp but will still be edible. Marcella's version is the technique-perfect version; the shortcut works for modern eggplants in most cases.

=== 1.5 INCHES OF OIL IS A LOT — SHALLOW-FRY, NOT SAUTÉ ===

Marcella specifies the depth. This is a proper shallow-fry, not a pan-sauté. The volume of oil is what gives the eggplant its crisp exterior. Neutral vegetable oil (not olive) — the fry is too aggressive for olive oil's flavor to survive intact, and the eggplant is the flavor carrier here.

=== ADD FRIED EGGPLANT AT THE END — DON'T LET IT COOK MORE IN THE SAUCE ===

The whole point of the shallow-fry is to give the eggplant a crisp exterior and creamy interior. If you fold it into the sauce and simmer, it turns to mush. Fold in at the end, off heat or brief tossing, and serve immediately.

=== SPAGHETTINI IS MARCELLA'S PAIRING ===

Thinner than spaghetti, thicker than capellini. The thinner strand carries the fried eggplant + garlic-tomato sauce cleanly without competing.

=== VARIANT B (RICOTTA + BASIL) DIFFERENCES FROM VARIANT A ===

- WHOLE TOMATOES (not diced): whole tomatoes crush and simmer down into a more integrated sauce; diced tomatoes read chunkier. Marcella prefers whole for the richer version. Crush by hand or with a spoon as they cook.
- SMALLER EGGPLANT CUBES (not slices): cubes distribute more evenly through the pasta than slices. Still salt/drain/fry them the same way — just cut smaller.
- OMITS CHILI FLAKES: the ricotta + basil register doesn't want heat competing with it. The dish reads cleaner and more delicate this way.
- FRESH RICOTTA + BASIL AT THE END: ricotta folded in (or dolloped) with the pasta, basil torn on top. Both raw, off heat. Pushes the dish toward the pasta-alla-norma / napoli-eggplant-pasta register without being strictly a norma (which uses salted ricotta salata rather than fresh, and doesn't add basil the same way).

=== SIBLING RECIPES (TOMATO PASTA SAUCE TAG) ===

- [[marcella-tomato-sauce]]: Marcella's 3-ingredient tomato + butter + onion. The simplest expression of the family.
- [[sicilian-pesto-rosso]]: raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond pesto.
- [[vodka-sauce]]: tomato paste + cream outlier.
- [[pasta-piperade]]: blended vegetable-tomato base.
